newsitem.title: UK: BRADYS CONTINUE INEXORABLE CLIMB, EXCEPT BULGARIA.
newsitem.headline: BRADYS CONTINUE INEXORABLE CLIMB, EXCEPT BULGARIA.

text.p: The relentless rise in emerging debt prices continued in Friday morning trade, though Bulgaria alone stuck to its own downward spiral.
Traders said Russia was the chief focus of the morning.
Vneshekonombank dollar paper touched fresh record highs in early trading, reaching 65-3/8 cents in the dollar, though it later slipped back a little.
The paper is being pushed up in anticipation of a credit rating for Russia's Eurobond, expected to be at the upper end of the speculative grade.
Though likely to be below Russia's own ambitious hopes, traders said a rating of around BB is likely, possibly towards the end of this month.
"For the moment people are discounting (President Boris) Yeltsin's health," one trader said.
Yeltsin's doctors have said they will seek Western advice about the 65-year old Kremlin leader's planned heart bypass operation.
Doctors are expected to decide the date of the operation at a meeting at the end of this month.
Latin American debt is also very firm though activity was fairly subdued in London trading.

Bulgaria, however, is having trouble picking up many takers though several traders continue to promote it as a cheap buy despite its economic shambles and delay in an International Monetary Fund loan.

"We retain the view that the IMF takes its obligations seriously; it is putting maximum pressure on Bulgaria to speed reforms, likely to be in place well before the next Brady repayment in January," ANZ analyst Jerome Booth said.
"Bulgarian IABs should be bought on further dips, though nervousness will continue until October," he added.
Some traders said there were signs that new money was continuing to come into the market, whose strength has come in spite of less sparkling U.S. Treasuries.
ANZ's Booth said the approach of the next U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on September 24 made it a good time to focus on high-yield emerging debt.
Nigeria is expected to rise further, partly on the back of higher oil prices, he added.
